title: Sparse probe playground & observability personas - lab notes
content:
Purpose and scope:
This doc collects exploratory notes for a compact, persona-driven observability prototype aimed at reducing signal noise and trace costs across LLM inference paths. Outcome goal: a small set of sparse probes and dashboard personas that give on-call and SRE teams high-confidence diagnosis signals for 80% of common regressions while keeping trace sampling budget under 10% of peak ingestion cost.

Key constraints (working assumptions):
- Multi-tenant inference with mixed short/long prompt distributions.
- KV prefix cache can make 40–60% of requests fast (TFT), but cold-cache tails remain high cost.
- Trace retention and query costs are dominant; need to trade off fidelity vs. coverage.
- Team resources limited: prefer low-friction dashboards and a small runbook rather than deep new tooling.

Personas (why they matter):
- Pager (oncall SRE/operator): wants a single-pane view to know if incident is cache, infra, or model quality. Needs clear SLO deviation + top-2 likely causes.
- Platform Eng (capacity/throughput owner): needs throughput & batching heatmaps, queue depth, burst surface.
- Product/SE (feature owner): wants output-quality regression signals (per-prompt evals, user cohorts).
- Observability Stewards (metric curators): maintain metric contracts, decide probe on/off.

Sparse probe strategy (playground ideas):
- Probe tiers:
  * Canary probes (every minute) — synthetic short prompt to each model variant + region. Lightweight, measure TFT, TTF, token throughput.
  * Session warmth probes (sampled per tenant) — edge probe that replays user-like prefixes to test KV-warmth behavior on key paths.
  * Error-path probes (on-sample) — when a request returns >1% bad-status / mismatch heuristics, attach a lightweight trace anchor (no full span dump).
  * Random trace-sampling slider — stratified: 0.5% baseline + 10% of error-paths + 5% of long-seqs (>2k tokens).

Metric budget and cardinality rules (practical heuristics):
- Budget by cardinality tier:
  * Tier A (global/system): 0–10 dimensions, high-frequency (1s) retention 14d. Examples: cluster-cpu, gpu-util, request-rate, serving-p99-latency.
  * Tier B (tenant-cohort): up to 50 cardinality; 1m resolution; retention 30d. Examples: tenant-pct-cold-cache, tenant-tail-latency-95.
  * Tier C (individual request attributes): sampled metrics only; retention 7d; use sketches or count-min where needed.
- Naming: <surface>.<unit>.<slice> e.g., serving.latency_ms.p50, kvcache.hit_rate.tenant_cohort. Keep names short and programmatic.
- Avoid high-cardinality joins in dashboards — flatten where reasonable (e.g., map tenant->cohort label upstream).

Tracing anchors and lightweight spans:
- Opt for short breadcrumb spans at key handoff points instead of full spans for every token:
  * client->ingress (request id, tenant, prompt_len)
  * routing decision (model_id, variant, queue_shard)
  * batch start/end (batch_size, estimated tokens)
  * model call summary (seq_len, kv_hit_fraction, first_token_latency)
- If an error or QoR check fails, upgrade with a single detailed model-sidespan (dump minimal KV diagnostic + truncated logits snapshot). This is gated by sampling + error heuristics.

Dashboard sketches (operator-first):
- Incident top of dashboard: SLO breaching indicator + auto-suggested hypotheses (cache cold / GPU saturated / model regression) with confidence score from rule heuristics.
- Lower panels:
  * Heatmap: first_token_latency by tenant_cohort vs hour_of_day (fast triage for bursts).
  * Waterfall: median/95/99 for serving.latency_ms.* with correlated gpu_util, batch_size time series aligned.
  * Probe panel: recent canary results table (status, delta_vs_baseline, utc_ts).
  * Trace-sampling budget meter: budget used today vs rolling 30d mean.

Runbook excerpts (quick action items):
- If TFT p99 jumps but probes green -> likely tenant cold cache. Action: check kvcache.eviction_rate and recent tenant-traffic pattern; consider prewarm policy for heavy tenants.
- If TFT and canary both spike -> model_variant/regional capacity issue. Action: check shard queue depth -> scale or fallback.
- If output-quality alerts + no latency signal -> test small eval suite against latest model build; if regression, rollback variant.

Operational experiments to run (A/B style):
- Sampling elasticity trial: gradually increase baseline trace sampling from 0.5% to 2% for two weeks on low-risk region to measure diagnostic uplift vs cost.
- Probe attenuation experiment: double canary cadence for 48 hours around deployments to understand sensitivity.
- Cohort compression: map top-100 tenants to 8 cohorts and measure signal loss on common alerts (target <5% deviation).

Open questions / TODOs:
- How to reliably attach tenant->cohort mapping upstream without leaking PII? Need legal/product input.
- Which QE checks should trigger automatic trace upgrade? Propose: non-200, hallucination score > threshold, perplexity spike.
- Needs: small demo dashboard for oncall run-through, and a cost model showing trace-dollar impact for different sampling policies.

Notes to self / rough timeline:
- Nov–Dec: prototype canary + heatmap panels; map tenant cohort offline.
- Jan: sampling elasticity trial + oncall tabletop.
- Feb: iterate on probe rules and add QA triggers.

References and related artifacts:
- Quick sketch board: https://figma.com/file/obs-playground/sketch-1 (internal)
- OBS-PLAYGROUND-93 confluence draft (linked above)

Author notes (informal):
- Keep the probe set intentionally small — operators get overwhelmed fast. Aim for 6–8 primary widgets per persona.
- Avoid metric proliferation by having small review gates (obs stewards sign-off) before exposing anything Tier B+.

Feedback welcome: ping me (Aisha) or drop notes into JIRA OBS-4123.
